name: Witch Doctor: Spirit Striker raises the Serpent Ward's Voodoo Fire proc chance (#824)
contract: #824: Spirit Striker 806286 carries ADD_FLAT_MODIFIER (aura 107), EffectMiscValue 18 (SPELLMOD_CHANCE_OF_SUCCESS), EffectBasePoints 9 (real value 10), EffectSpellClassMask word1 bit 27 (134217728), matching exactly the SpellFamilyFlags[1] of Voodoo Fire One 802262 (ProcChance 20) and Voodoo Fire Two 803846 (ProcChance 40). The Serpent Ward's UpdateAI (AscensionWitchDoctorSummons.cpp) rolled that chance as a hardcoded C++ literal (20 or 40) via roll_chance_f, never through Player::ApplySpellMod, so the registered spellmod was silently dropped -- a real_bug (Spirit Striker's +10% had zero gameplay effect). The fix adds player->ApplySpellMod(VoodooFireOne/Two, SPELLMOD_CHANCE_OF_SUCCESS, chance) before the roll, matching the existing pattern in AscensionPrimalistJudgement.cpp/AscensionPyromancerEvents.cpp. spell_modifier on VoodooFireOne is NOT usable proof here: the aura is a plain core-generic ADD_FLAT_MODIFIER, so it registers on the player identically before and after the fix -- it only proves the aura loaded, not that the pet code consults it (this is the exact trap the investigation flagged). The gameplay-test harness also has no metric that can attribute a spell cast or spell-damage event to a player-owned TempSummon actor: spell_cast_count/spell_proc_count key off GetUnit(actor), which only resolves to a player (_actors) or a harness 'creatures' fixture (_targets), and spell_go_count/spell_damage_count/spell_damage_total require the actor to BE a player and restrict 'caster' to that player's own GUID or Player::GetPetGUID() (a formal pet); the Serpent Ward is summoned via Player::SummonCreature + SetOwnerGUID, never registered as a formal Pet or as a harness target, so none of those metrics can isolate its casts (confirmed by reading modules/mod-ascension-compat/src/CoAGameplayTest.cpp, not assumed). The only available proof is therefore statistical: the enemy fixture's own health loss, compared in the same run before vs after learning 806286, over N=140 Serpent Ward attack ticks per phase (WardAttackInterval=2000ms, no haste). Voodoo Fire (500473, EffectBasePoints 72, no per-level scaling) fires only on a successful roll; Serpent Ward Attack (573055, EffectBasePoints 4 + EffectRealPointsPerLevel 2.3 -> about 186 at level 80) fires every tick regardless, so it dominates the mean damage and dilutes the ratio signal: with p=0.2 to p=0.3 the expected ratio of phase-2-to-phase-1 health loss is only around 1.036 by this rough theoretical calculation (not measured on a live server); 1.02 is used as a deliberately conservative pass/fail line, closer to the unfixed side than the midpoint, so a false PASS on unfixed code is rarer than a false FAIL on fixed code. This statistical distinguisher was designed from DBC constants only (BasePoints, ProcChance, RealPointsPerLevel) and was NOT executed against a live worldserver (out of scope for this task, no build/deploy performed); it does not account for the Serpent Ward's own possible spell-crit chance or partial magic-resist rolls against the fixture, both unverified, so the true false-pass/false-fail rate could exceed the theoretical ~15% two-sided estimate documented in fix-824.md. It is included as the best available same-run, server-numbers regression signal given this constraint, not as a low-flake guarantee. Hex of Malice 501158 is cast once purely to put the caster in combat with the enemy fixture (Unit::SetInCombatWith on the original caster is required for AscensionWitchDoctor::Enemy() to ever hand the ward a target) and its own damage (instant hit + a 24000 ms DOT, SpellDuration.dbc row 106) is fully waited out before either measured phase begins, so it never contaminates the comparison.

steps.label: No damage bonus on Voodoo Fire One before Spirit Striker (registration sanity check, not proof of consumption)
Let the ward settle before entering combat
Hex of Malice puts the caster in combat with the fixture
Let Hex of Malice's instant hit and 24000 ms DOT fully resolve before measuring
The ward survived the settle window
PHASE 1 (no Spirit Striker): 140 Serpent Ward ticks at 2000 ms
Voodoo Fire One's registered spellmod is still 30 after learning Spirit Striker (registration sanity check, not proof of consumption)
PHASE 2 (with Spirit Striker): another 140 Serpent Ward ticks at 2000 ms

FIX PROOF: with Spirit Striker learned, phase 2 health loss is at least 2% larger than phase 1's own same-run baseline. Before the fix this ratio stays flat around 1.0 (the hardcoded 20% roll never moves); after the fix the boosted 30% roll pushes it toward ~1.036.
